input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production; merge when done.
task: Deepen (flagship 7): photo-editing -- read Canon CR3 directly

errors.what: Early CRX run-mode readings decoded only 3-4 lines
errors.fix: bisected with LibRaw raw values as oracle; brute-forcing run index and Rice K at the failing line showed the run flag bit counts as one sample

errors.what: After a mutation check the restored cr3.py failed tests
errors.fix: stale __pycache__: same size and same-second mtime as the mutant; cleared it

errors.what: mypy (photo-editing-ci lint) flagged Cmp1(bytes | None) three times
errors.fix: Container keeps the parsed CMP1 as .head; ruff and mypy clean in a numpy-free venv as CI runs them

doc_friction.issue: photo-editing buildable said raw.pixls.us 'answers since 2026-11-15'; from this container it answered 403 (CONNECT tunnel refused) on 2026-11-15. Rewrote the line to say so.
_AS_SHOT_INDEX comment lists ColorData8-11 but the table stops at ColorData10; CR3 bodies' ColorData11 lengths (3778, 3973) are added in cr3.py

30 tests used IMG_0001.CR3 as the 'raw we do not develop' fixture with hard-coded graded names; supporting a format silently broke them. Now no ingested RAW extension is undevelopable by extension; the stop-at-grade test uses a synthetic C-RAW CR3.

deviations.why: next: listed newer CR2s from raw.pixls.us, unreachable here; took full-quality CR3 (the format every Canon since 2018 writes) from the reachable metadata-extractor-images set instead
deviations.did: new shootflow.cr3 reader, C twin, tests, eval, post
deviations.result: 0 of 25.5M sensels differ from LibRaw on both full-quality R8 files

goal: Deepen the photo-editing flagship: CR3 is the raw format of every Canon body since 2018
notes: tools/cr3_libraw_check.py on the 5 public CR3s: IMG_0036 and _MG_0039 (EOS R8, lossless) 0 sensels differing with C and Python, balance/CFA/white equal, black within 1; IMG_0041, _MG_0045, Canon EOS R3 (C-RAW) refused with reason. tests/test_cr3.py 12 OK with and without the C path. run_venture_tests.py photo-editing: ok, 0 failed, 8 skipped (151.5 s); a first run failed 30 planner/pipeline tests that used .CR3 as their undevelopable-raw fixture, updated to expect .CR3.tif graded names and a C-RAW CR3 for the stop-at-grade test. run_workflow_locally --for-changes: 13/15 passed; photo-editing-ci lint failed on mypy (fixed, rechecked clean); its test step UNRUN locally (no Pillow in system python) but run_venture_tests ran it green; portfolio-pages build/deploy and reviewer bots not run locally.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an experienced imaging engineer reverse-checking a raw codec and container against LibRaw, plus tests and integration: about three days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
